findings.reason: the author would drop §2f as pending and record it landed, and route any residual change through the lane_document.py owner.
findings.text: §2f's done-when ("a lane document is reported field by field, each present value carried and each absent one marked absent … requiring headroom to read 4 rather than unknown") describes behaviour already shipped by `read_lane_reading_fields` and `dispatch._lane_reading_carry` (dispatch.py:3916, commit 1a64dede3 "a lane reading withholds the figure it cannot read, not all of them", ancestor of HEAD); the plan cites the stale site `dispatch.py:1890` and never names lane_document.py, so a node dispatched from this done-when would rebuild a landed fix.

findings.reason: the author would verify the landed behaviour and either close §2g or narrow it to the one unmet clause (the refusal reporting which inputs it counted and their sizes).
findings.text: §2g's done-when ("a file named only in prose is not charged … a declared write path is still charged") describes behaviour already shipped by `_context_file_inputs`, which charges only `_declared_input_files` and skips prose mentions (commit 318ec2b6a "count only declared files toward a node's context estimate", ancestor of HEAD); the plan proposes the fix as pending without noting it is in.

findings.reason: the author would either extend `by_capability_class` with the lane-admission verdict or state why that overlay cannot carry it, which decides whether the change is a config-schema extension or a new parallel mechanism.
findings.text: §2 adds a per-class lane-admission rule "in the flight configuration beside the backend it governs" with no justification for a new key; flight config already validates and resolves per-class overlays `by_capability_class` and `by_spec_level` for exactly this role/lane routing, and the plan's own §2 text says the rule is read "where the role and spec level are already resolved" — the resolution point it names is the existing overlay.

findings.reason: the author would extend promotion.py's existing predicate rather than specify a second flag, removing a duplicate owner for one gate.
findings.text: §2's done-when asks for "a review-required flag that `crew complete` honours by refusing promotion without a scored review from another lane", but promotion.py already owns that gate: `_refuse_unreviewed_promotion` computes a `review_required` predicate and refuses an unreviewed promotable run, and the plan's own §3 comment records that `crew complete` already refuses an unreviewed promotion and names the review it wants.

findings.reason: the author would either fold the five prescription properties into node.py's validator (the owner of node-property judgement and the D07 refusal renderer) or record why the lane-fitness verdict must be a separate judge over one node record.
findings.text: §2's `judge_prescribed` re-implements node-property judgement that node.py already owns: `negative_control_finding` (node.py:975) plus `NEGATIVE_CONTROL_FIELD`/`is_test_path`/`parse_duration` are the node's negative-control and fence properties, and `validate_node` (node.py:1103) already returns a `NodeValidation.findings` list reporting every failed property, while prescription.py returns a parallel `{prescribed, failures, detail}` structure over the same record and imports node.py's helpers.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `judge_prescribed` (prescription.py:130) hides five properties behind one function returning a three-key verdict, and lane_document.read_lane_reading_fields hides the field resolution behind one call; the design does not spread complexity across shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2's "review-required flag that crew complete honours" duplicates the review gate promotion.py already owns, and §2's one-artifact/negative-control properties duplicate the node-property judge node.py already owns.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan proposes §2f per-field lane reading and §2g prose-vs-declared context charging, both of which already exist in the tree (reckon/crew/lane_document.py and routing.py `_context_file_inputs`), and cites neither owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2 proposes a per-class lane-admission rule in flight config without saying why the existing `by_capability_class` / `by_spec_level` dispatch overlay (flight.py:974) cannot carry it.
